articles.title: ​​Homo erectus and Denisovans may have lived alongside each other in China, study suggests
articles.author: Chris Simms

paras.en: Homo erectus was adaptable enough to live in rainforests in what is now southern China and may have lived alongside Denisovans there, two new studies hint.
paras.zh: 两项新研究暗示，直立人的适应能力足以生活在现在中国南部的雨林中，并且可能与那里的丹尼索瓦人一起生活。

paras.en: The research is based on the incredibly rare findings of nine fossil teeth from ancient humans — eight from H. erectus and one from a mystery human in the genus Homo. The teeth reveal that H. erectus lived in China much more recently than previously thought and that this population likely devoured tropical food found there.
paras.zh: 这项研究基于对古代人类九颗牙齿化石的极其罕见的发现——其中八颗来自直立人，一颗来自人属的神秘人类。这些牙齿表明，直立人生活在中国的时间比之前想象的要晚得多，而且这个种群很可能吞食那里发现的热带食物。

paras.en: "I think it's exciting because it means that there are two hominin populations occupying these rainforest conditions there at the same time," study first author Frido Welker, a molecular palaeoanthropologist at the University of Copenhagen in Denmark, told Live Science.
paras.zh: 研究第一作者、丹麦哥本哈根大学分子古人类学家弗里多·韦尔克 (Frido Welker) 告诉《生活科学》杂志：“我认为这很令人兴奋，因为这意味着有两个古人类种群同时占据了这些雨林条件。”

paras.en: H. erectus is generally seen as the first human species to venture out of Africa, after evolving about 2 million years ago. It spread through eastern Eurasia, reaching China and Indonesia between about 1.6 million and 1.8 million years ago. It is one of the longest-surviving hominin species, and the last known record of it is from 108,000 years ago in river flood plains in Java, Indonesia. However, there was no physical evidence of H. erectus being on the Asian mainland more recently than 400,000 years ago.
paras.zh: 直立人通常被视为第一个走出非洲的人类物种，经过大约 200 万年前的进化。它穿过欧亚大陆东部，在大约 160 万至 180 万年前到达中国和印度尼西亚。它是现存最长寿的人类物种之一，其最后的已知记录是 108,000 年前在印度尼西亚爪哇河漫滩上发现的。然而，没有任何物理证据表明直立人在 40 万年前就曾出现在亚洲大陆。

paras.en: But in two caves in Guangxi province in southern China, researchers have found thousands of mammalian fossils, accumulated there by porcupines that scavenged for and collected bones. The Baxian and Naxian caves are about 9 miles (15 kilometers) apart, sitting in a karst landscape of limestone formations that are prone to dissolving to create caves that would have offered crucial shelter for H. erectus.
paras.zh: 但在中国南部广西省的两个洞穴中，研究人员发现了数千个哺乳动物化石，这些化石是由豪猪在其中寻找和收集骨头而积累的。巴仙洞穴和纳仙洞穴相距约 9 英里（15 公里），坐落在石灰岩地貌的喀斯特地貌中，这些石灰岩地层很容易溶解形成洞穴，为直立人提供了重要的庇护所。

paras.en: Researchers found the nine human teeth among more than 18,000 fossils, including from apes, elephants, rhinoceroses and other ancient hoofed animals, Welker and his colleagues reported in a study published Wednesday (Nov. 18) in the journal Nature.
paras.zh: 韦尔克和他的同事在周三（11 月 18 日）《自然》杂志上发表的一项研究中报告说，研究人员在 18,000 多块化石中发现了 9 颗人类牙齿，这些化石包括猿、大象、犀牛和其他古代有蹄动物。

paras.en: Radiometric dating of the fossils and surrounding sediments by methods including assessing the decay of uranium, pins them to about 324,000 to 184,000 years ago. Eight of the teeth have physical features reminiscent of H. erectus, but the ninth is more elusive. It looks distinct from H. erectus, Neanderthals and modern humans, Welker said.
paras.zh: 通过评估铀衰变等方法对化石和周围沉积物进行放射性测年，将其确定为大约 324,000 至 184,000 年前。其中八颗牙齿的物理特征让人想起直立人，但第九颗牙齿则更加难以捉摸。韦尔克说，它看起来与直立人、尼安德特人和现代人类不同。

paras.en: Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
paras.zh: 将世界上最迷人的发现直接发送到您的收件箱。

paras.en: Welker's team took samples from five teeth — four from the group that seemed to be H. erectus and one from the mysterious tooth — to see which ancient proteins were present, since DNA tends to degrade more easily than the proteins in an organism. (The study of these proteins is known as proteomics.)
paras.zh: 韦尔克的团队从五颗牙齿中采集了样本——其中四颗来自似乎是直立人的牙齿，一颗来自神秘的牙齿——来看看存在哪些古老的蛋白质，因为DNA往往比生物体中的蛋白质更容易降解。 （对这些蛋白质的研究称为蛋白质组学。）

paras.en: The four similar ones had protein signatures that matched what had been seen before in H. erectus.
paras.zh: 这四个相似的蛋白质特征与之前在直立人中看到的特征相匹配。

paras.en: "The morphology is nicely confirmed by the proteomics," Welker told Live Science. Three of these teeth were from males, and the other was from a female, which the team was able to determine based on the presence or absence of amelogenin-Y, a protein coded for only by the Y chromosome.
paras.zh: “蛋白质组学很好地证实了这种形态，”韦尔克告诉《生活科学》。其中三颗牙齿来自男性，另一颗来自女性，研究小组能够根据牙釉蛋白-Y（一种仅由 Y 染色体编码的蛋白质）是否存在来确定。

paras.en: However, some parts of the protein signatures differed from what had been seen in other H. erectus remains in China, so the new specimens may be from a previously unknown H. erectus population that perhaps had a slightly different genetic makeup, Welker said.
paras.zh: 然而，蛋白质特征的某些部分与中国其他直立人遗骸中发现的不同，因此新标本可能来自以前未知的直立人种群，该种群的基因组成可能略有不同，韦尔克说。

paras.en: The finding that H. erectus was present in mainland Asia until at least 184,000 years ago — rather than 400,000 years ago — fills a geographical and chronological gap, helping to explain how H. erectus was on Java 108,000 years ago.
paras.zh: 直立人至少在 184,000 年前（而不是 400,000 年前）就存在于亚洲大陆，这一发现填补了地理和时间上的空白，有助于解释 108,000 年前直立人是如何在爪哇岛存在的。

paras.en: "This brings the history of H. erectus in East Asia closer in age to the late Javanese examples, raising the possibility that these populations were connected through land bridges at times of lowered sea level," Chris Stringer, a paleoanthropologist at the Natural History Museum in London who was not involved in the research, told Live Science in an email.
paras.zh: 伦敦自然历史博物馆的古人类学家克里斯·斯金格（Chris Stringer）没有参与这项研究，他在一封电子邮件中告诉《生活科学》杂志：“这使得东亚直立人的历史与爪哇晚期的例子更加接近，这增加了这些种群在海平面下降时期通过陆桥相连的可能性。”

paras.en: John Hawks, an anthropologist at the University of Wisconsin-Madison who wasn't involved in the study, previously believed that specimens from the past 400,000 years or so flagged as H. erectus were actually Denisovans — ancient humans who lived in Asia, disappeared around 30,000 years ago and belonged to the Homo longi lineage. But he told Live Science that the new morphological and protein findings provide convincing evidence that H. erectus did survive until relatively recently in some places.
paras.zh: 威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校的人类学家约翰·霍克斯（John Hawks）并未参与这项研究，他此前认为，过去 40 万年前被标记为直立人的标本实际上是丹尼索瓦人——生活在亚洲的古代人类，大约在 3 万年前消失，属于长人谱系。但他告诉《生活科学》杂志，新的形态和蛋白质发现提供了令人信服的证据，证明直立人直到最近才在某些地方生存。

paras.en: The fifth analyzed tooth, known as PA1796, remains mysterious. The protein analysis revealed it was from a male, but it didn't show a recognizable signature in the protein sequence data. Therefore, Welker's team suggested it could be from another hominin species that was present in the region at the same time.
paras.zh: 第五颗被分析的牙齿被称为 PA1796，仍然是个谜。蛋白质分析显示它来自男性，但蛋白质序列数据中没有显示出可识别的特征。因此，韦尔克的团队认为它可能来自同时存在于该地区的另一种古人类物种。

paras.en: Welker didn’t want to speculate about which species it might be, but said: "Sequence-wise it doesn't have this Homo erectus substitution and morphologically, it doesn't look like an erectus tooth."
paras.zh: 韦尔克不想猜测它可能是什么物种，但他说：“从序列上看，它没有这种直立人的替代，从形态上看，它看起来不像直立人的牙齿。”

paras.en: The tooth could be from a previously unknown human species, but many experts suspect it is from a Denisovan.
paras.zh: 这颗牙齿可能来自以前未知的人类物种，但许多专家怀疑它来自丹尼索瓦人。

paras.en: "With some of the new material probably dating to less than 200,000 years old, this already brings it close in age to known or putative Homo longi/Denisovan samples in southern China and Laos, implying potentially long overlaps between these species," Stringer said. "Tooth PA1796 could represent a longi/Denisovan, though it is relatively small in size, and relevant comparative data for longi/Denisovans is sparse."
paras.zh: 斯金格说：“由于一些新材料的历史可能不到20万年，这已经使其年龄与中国南部和老挝已知或推定的长人/丹尼索瓦人样本的年龄接近，这意味着这些物种之间可能存在长期重叠。” “牙齿 PA1796 可能代表长吉/丹尼索瓦人，尽管它的尺寸相对较小，而且长吉/丹尼索瓦人的相关比较数据很少。”

paras.en: Recent research suggests there was interbreeding between the H. erectus and Denisovan lineages, and the new evidence increases the likelihood that this happened, at least occasionally, Stringer said.
paras.zh: 斯特林格说，最近的研究表明直立人与丹尼索瓦人血统之间存在杂交，新的证据增加了这种情况发生的可能性，至少偶尔发生。

paras.en: Any firm conclusions of who the tooth is from will have to wait for further finds of similar teeth elsewhere, Welker said.
paras.zh: 韦尔克说，关于这颗牙齿来自谁的任何确切结论都必须等待在其他地方进一步发现类似的牙齿。

paras.en: Hawks agreed that the tooth is most likely from a Denisovan, perhaps from a divergent branch for which we don't have protein data. But it could also be from a novel H. erectus population or someone from the same population as the other teeth who, for developmental or genetic reasons, wasn't typical. "I would have liked to see additional comparisons in the paper to more Denisovan teeth," Hawks said.
paras.zh: 霍克斯一致认为，这颗牙齿很可能来自丹尼索瓦人，也许来自我们没有蛋白质数据的不同分支。但它也可能来自一个新的直立人种群，或者来自与其他牙齿相同种群的人，但由于发育或遗传原因，这些牙齿并不典型。 “我希望在论文中看到与更多丹尼索瓦人牙齿的更多比较，”霍克斯说。

paras.en: In another paper, also published Nov. 18 in the journal Nature, Kira Westaway, a geochronologist at Macquarie University in Sydney, and her colleagues examined trace elements in the same teeth, as well as in animal teeth from the caves, to see what they revealed about the hominins' diet and local habitat.
paras.zh: 在另一篇同样发表在 11 月 18 日《自然》杂志上的论文中，悉尼麦格理大学的地质年代学家 Kira Westaway 和她的同事检查了相同牙齿以及洞穴中动物牙齿中的微量元素，以了解它们对古人类饮食和当地栖息地的揭示。

paras.en: Their analysis indicated that this H. erectus population found plants and animals to eat in tropical, rainforest-like ecosystems. Previously, it was thought that only our own species, Homo sapiens, was able to adapt to this type of environment.
paras.zh: 他们的分析表明，直立人种群在热带雨林式生态系统中找到了可食用的植物和动物。此前，人们认为只有我们自己的物种——智人——能够适应这种环境。

paras.en: "Rather than being confined to open woodland and grassland environments, H. erectus was considerably more ecologically adaptable than many of us have assumed," Stringer said.
paras.zh: “直立人并不局限于开阔的林地和草原环境，它的生态适应性比我们许多人想象的要强得多，”斯特林格说。

paras.en: "Being adaptable and being flexible are not traits that we associate with ancient human species — these are traits that we associate with H. sapiens," Westaway told Live Science. "Suddenly we're seeing H. erectus being able to survive in environments that we didn't think they could possibly survive in."
paras.zh: “适应能力和灵活性并不是我们与古代人类物种相关的特征，而是我们与智人相关的特征，”韦斯特韦告诉《生活科学》。 “突然间，我们看到直立人能够在我们认为它们不可能生存的环境中生存。”

paras.en: And given the mysterious tooth, it is possible that two different early human populations were this adaptable, said Welker, who was a co-author of the study.
paras.zh: 该研究的合著者韦尔克说，考虑到这颗神秘的牙齿，两个不同的早期人类群体可能具有如此强的适应性。

paras.en: Westaway and her colleagues also looked at levels of the element strontium in the teeth, which can shed light on where someone grew up based on the unique strontium levels in water and foods they consumed as children. The team matched these strontium levels to another karst landscape about 200 miles (320 km) away, in the Red River valley of northern Vietnam.
paras.zh: 韦斯特韦和她的同事还研究了牙齿中锶元素的含量，这可以根据一个人小时候所喝的水和食物中独特的锶含量来了解一个人在哪里长大。研究小组将这些锶含量与约 200 英里（320 公里）外、越南北部红河谷的另一个喀斯特地貌相匹配。

paras.en: "It looks like H. erectus moved across large areas, traversing this karst landscape in the rainforests" — a finding that adds to our understanding of these ancient humans, Westaway said.
paras.zh: 韦斯特韦说：“看起来直立人跨越了大片区域，穿越了雨林中的喀斯特地貌”——这一发现增加了我们对这些古代人类的了解。

paras.en: - 'Absolute surprise': Homo erectus skulls found in China are almost 1.8 million years old — the oldest evidence of the ancient human relatives in East Asia
paras.zh: -“绝对令人惊讶”：在中国发现的直立人头骨已有近 180 万年的历史——东亚古代人类亲戚的最古老证据

paras.en: - Our extinct cousins the Denisovans had a 'distinctive' appearance, new analysis reveals
paras.zh: - 新的分析显示，我们已灭绝的表亲丹尼索瓦人具有“独特”的外观

paras.en: - Neanderthal DNA still survives in our human family tree. What were our ancient relatives' relationships like?
paras.zh: - 尼安德特人的 DNA 仍然存在于我们人类的家谱中。我们古代的亲戚关系是怎样的？

paras.en: It's absurd that people often think of H. erectus as an unsuccessful species, she added. "We think they were the first to leave Africa, the first to use fire. It blows my mind because they survived six times longer than H. sapiens has survived so far, so I don't see them as unsuccessful."
paras.zh: 她补充说，人们常常认为直立人是一个不成功的物种，这是荒谬的。 “我们认为他们是第一个离开非洲的人，第一个使用火的人。这让我大吃一惊，因为他们的生存时间是智人迄今为止生存时间的六倍，所以我不认为他们是不成功的。”

paras.en: Hawks' big question, however, is linked to modern humans, who were in the Chinese region from at least 45,000 years ago.
paras.zh: 然而，霍克斯的大问题与现代人类有关，现代人类至少在 45,000 年前就生活在中国地区。

paras.en: "Denisovan DNA is present in the peoples of Island Southeast Asia, so, modern humans must have run into Denisovans at some point," he said. "If H. erectus was enduring in the same area at the same time, might H. sapiens also have encountered late H. erectus?"
paras.zh: “丹尼索瓦人的 DNA 存在于东南亚岛屿的人民中，因此，现代人类一定在某个时候遇到了丹尼索瓦人，”他说。 “如果直立人同时在同一地区生存，那么智人是否也遇到了晚期直立人？”

paras.en: What do you know about early humans? Test your knowledge with our human origins quiz!
paras.zh: 关于早期人类，你了解多少？通过我们的人类起源测验测试您的知识！

paras.en: Chris Simms is a freelance journalist who previously worked at New Scientist for more than 10 years, in roles including chief subeditor and assistant news editor. He was also a senior subeditor at Nature and has a degree in zoology from Queen Mary University of London. In recent years, he has written numerous articles for New Scientist and in 2018 was shortlisted for Best Newcomer at the Association of British Science Writers awards.
paras.zh: 克里斯·西姆斯 (Chris Simms) 是一名自由撰稿人，曾在《新科学家》杂志工作了 10 多年，担任过首席副主编和助理新闻编辑等职务。他还是《自然》杂志的高级副编辑，并拥有伦敦玛丽女王大学动物学学位。近年来，他为《新科学家》撰写了大量文章，并于2018年入围英国科学作家协会奖最佳新人奖。

articles.title: Medieval Readers Saw Floods, Plagues and Comets as Omens of Doom—So They Created a Mysterious Manuscript of Apocalyptic Artworks to Peruse at Will

paras.en: In the Bible, God’s will often emerges through natural phenomena. The great flood cleanses the earth of human corruption, while the rainbow symbolizes the divine covenant “between God and every living creature.” For millennia, worshippers familiar with these stories have wondered: What meaning can be found in the movements of storms, seas and stars?
paras.zh: 在圣经中，神的旨意常常通过自然现象显现出来。大洪水净化了地球上的人类腐败，而彩虹则象征着“上帝与所有生物之间”的神圣契约。几千年来，熟悉这些故事的崇拜者一直在想：风暴、海洋和星星的运动有何意义？

paras.en: That’s the central question of The Book of Miracles, an illustrated manuscript dating to the mid-16th century. Featuring 167 imaginative paintings, the text begins with episodes from the Old Testament and ends with apocalyptic visions from the Book of Revelation. Between them is a catalog of earthquakes, comet sightings, locust plagues, volcanic eruptions and other events spanning antiquity through the manuscript’s creation.
paras.zh: 这是《奇迹之书》的核心问题，这是一本可追溯至 16 世纪中叶的插图手稿。该文本以 167 幅富有想象力的画作为特色，以《旧约》中的情节开始，以《启示录》中的世界末日景象结束。在它们之间是一系列地震、彗星目击、蝗灾、火山爆发和手稿创作过程中跨越古代的其他事件的目录。

paras.en: Now, The Book of Miracles is heading to the auction block, where it’s expected to fetch between roughly $920,000 and $1.3 million. Bidders can vie for the volume during Christie’s Valuable Books and Manuscripts sale on December 10.
paras.zh: 现在，《奇迹之书》正在拍卖，预计售价约为 92 万至 130 万美元。竞标者可以在 12 月 10 日的佳士得珍贵书籍和手稿拍卖会上争夺该书。

paras.en: “The artists of The Book of Miracles have reinterpreted historical and contemporary sources with apocalyptic panache,” per the lot listing. Illustrations of earthquakes, floods and other natural disasters that occurred in Europe are “among the most energetic, imaginative and colorful illustrations in the manuscript.”
paras.zh: 拍品清单上写道：“《奇迹之书》的艺术家们以世界末日般的气派重新诠释了历史和当代的资料。”欧洲发生的地震、洪水和其他自然灾害的插图是“手稿中最有活力、最富有想象力和色彩缤纷的插图之一”。

paras.en: The text was rediscovered in the library of a Bavarian castle about two decades ago. It’s since changed hands several times. After acquiring the manuscript, London art dealer James Faber helped date it to the 16th century. The publisher Taschen released a facsimile edition in 2013.
paras.zh: 大约二十年前，该文本在巴伐利亚城堡的图书馆中被重新发现。此后它又易手数次。伦敦艺术品经销商詹姆斯·费伯 (James Faber) 获得这份手稿后，帮助确定其年代为 16 世纪。出版商 Taschen 于 2013 年发行了传真版。

paras.en: Because The Book of Miracles depicts about a dozen events near Augsburg, a city in modern-day Germany, scholars think it may have been created there. Christie’s attributes the manuscript to two painters, Hans Burgkmair the Younger and Heinrich Vogtherr the Younger, and their workshops. Nobody knows who commissioned the manuscript—or what exactly that individual had in mind. “Its existence was hitherto unknown, and silence wraps its discovery,” the New York Review of Books’ Marina Warner wrote in 2014. “This Book of Miracles is a gorgeous unheralded surprise: a foundling of unknown parents, a virgin birth.”
paras.zh: 由于《奇迹之书》描述了现代德国城市奥格斯堡附近的十几起事件，学者们认为它可能是在那里创作的。佳士得认为这份手稿的作者是两位画家：小汉斯·布格克迈尔 (Hans Burgkmair the Younger) 和小海因里希·沃格瑟尔 (Heinrich Vogtherr the Younger) 及其工作室。没有人知道是谁委托撰写了这份手稿，也不知道那个人到底有什么想法。 《纽约书评》的玛丽娜·华纳 (Marina Warner) 在 2014 年写道：“它的存在迄今无人知晓，沉默包裹着它的发现。”“这本奇迹之书是一个华丽的、意想不到的惊喜：一个未知父母的弃儿，一个处女的诞生。”

paras.en: The manuscript is divided into three parts. The Old Testament section features famous biblical scenes, including Moses parting the Red Sea and Jonah and the whale, while the Book of Revelation section depicts St. John’s apocalyptic visions. The middle section records historical events across the centuries, such as the eruption of Mount Vesuvius.
paras.zh: 手稿分为三个部分。旧约部分展示了著名的圣经场景，包括摩西分开红海和约拿与鲸鱼，而启示录部分则描绘了圣约翰的世界末日景象。中间部分记录了几个世纪以来的历史事件，例如维苏威火山的喷发。

paras.en: - The volcano famously demolished several Roman towns, including Pompeii and Herculaneum, in 79 C.E.
paras.zh: - 公元 79 年，这座火山摧毁了包括庞贝和赫库兰尼姆在内的数个罗马城镇，这一点众所周知。

paras.en: - The Book of Miracles incorrectly dates the eruption to 1482. Although Vesuvius has erupted repeatedly over many years, the manuscript mentions Pliny the Elder, who died in the 79 eruption. According to the caption, the Roman author had “wanted to see the fire but the fire consumed him too.”
paras.zh: - 《奇迹之书》错误地将喷发日期定为 1482 年。尽管维苏威火山多年来反复喷发，但手稿中提到了老普林尼，他在第 79 次喷发中丧生。根据标题，这位罗马作者“想看到火焰，但火焰也把他吞噬了”。

paras.en: Each image is accompanied by a caption in German. For example, the text below the Vesuvius illustration describes how the volcano “burst open at its summit or peak and threw up such a fire that cities and villages and all the trees burned up.” The latest event depicted in the manuscript is a 1552 hailstorm over the Dutch city of Dordrecht, so terrifying that “the people thought the Day of Judgment was coming.”
paras.zh: 每张图片都附有德语说明文字。例如，维苏威火山插图下面的文字描述了火山如何“在其顶峰或山峰爆发并喷出大火，烧毁了城市、村庄和所有树木”。手稿中描述的最新事件是 1552 年荷兰城市多德雷赫特的一场冰雹，这场冰雹非常可怕，以至于“人们认为审判日即将到来”。

paras.en: Some of the images from the middle section are fantastical—at least at first glance. One illustration depicts “wondrous dragons” crossing Bavaria’s skies in 1533; scholars think they may represent the northern lights. The five suns that “many trustworthy persons” saw over Leipzig in 1551 were likely an illusion known as a parhelion.
paras.zh: 中间部分的一些图像非常梦幻——至少乍一看是这样。一幅插图描绘了 1533 年穿越巴伐利亚天空的“神奇巨龙”；学者认为它们可能代表北极光。 1551 年，“许多值得信赖的人”在莱比锡上空看到的五个太阳很可能是一种被称为幻日点的幻觉。

paras.en: “Beyond their extraordinary beauty, these images offer us a glimpse into how people in the 16th century made sense of a world that could often seem mysterious and unpredictable,” Eugenio Donadoni, Christie’s specialist in medieval and Renaissance manuscripts, tells the Art Newspaper’s Maev Kennedy. “Today, we might understand a comet, an eclipse or an earthquake through science, but in the Renaissance, these phenomena could be interpreted as signs of something greater, even as warnings of what was to come.”
paras.zh: 佳士得中世纪和文艺复兴手稿专家尤金尼奥·多纳多尼 (Eugenio Donadoni) 告诉《艺术报》的梅夫·肯尼迪 (Maev Kennedy)，“除了非凡的美感之外，这些图像还让我们一睹 16 世纪的人们如何理解这个看似神秘且不可预测的世界。” “今天，我们可能通过科学来理解彗星、日食或地震，但在文艺复兴时期，这些现象可以被解释为更伟大事物的迹象，甚至是对即将发生的事情的警告。”

paras.en: According to the lot listing, the manuscript was influenced by illustrated broadsheets, or news bulletins that frequently covered strange celestial happenings. For readers who saw extreme weather as harbingers of horrors to come, “all of these events are portentous,” Donadoni tells the Guardian’s Donna Ferguson. Perusing The Book of Miracles may have been “a little like the 16th-century version of doomscrolling.”
paras.zh: 根据拍品清单，手稿受到插图大报或经常报道奇怪天体事件的新闻公告的影响。对于那些将极端天气视为即将到来的恐怖预兆的读者来说，“所有这些事件都是不祥的，”多纳多尼告诉卫报的唐娜·弗格森。细读《奇迹之书》可能“有点像 16 世纪版本的末日卷轴”。

paras.en: Nearly 500 years have passed since the manuscript’s creation, but humanity’s fascination with doom has endured. “One can easily imagine more recent catastrophes getting the Book of Miracles treatment, from people clinging to their rooftops in the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina in 2005 to scenes of almost biblical devastation following the tsunami generated by the Tohoku earthquake in 2011,” Collectors Weekly’s Ben Marks wrote in 2014. “That may be the real message of Book of Miracles, that the veneer of civilization we place our faith in daily is actually rather fragile and thin.”
paras.zh: 自手稿创作以来已经过去了近 500 年，但人类对末日的迷恋却一直存在。 《收藏家周刊》的本·马克斯 (Ben Marks) 在 2014 年写道：“人们可以很容易想象最近发生的灾难会受到《奇迹之书》的处理，从 2005 年卡特里娜飓风过后，人们紧贴屋顶，到 2011 年东北地震引发的海啸后几乎圣经中的毁灭场景。”“这可能是《奇迹之书》的真正信息，文明的外表我们日常所寄托的信仰其实是相当脆弱和单薄的。”

articles.title: A Gene Variant Inherited From Neanderthals Might Affect Modern Humans' Brain Size and Provide Protection Against Schizophrenia

paras.en: Tens of thousands of years ago, Homo sapiens interbred with Neanderthals, resulting in billions of humans alive today carrying traces of these extinct cousins in their DNA. The bits of Neanderthal ancestry can affect mood, metabolism, disease risk and other traits.
paras.zh: 数万年前，智人与尼安德特人杂交，导致今天活着的数十亿人的 DNA 中带有这些已灭绝近亲的痕迹。尼安德特人的血统会影响情绪、新陈代谢、疾病风险和其他特征。

paras.en: Now, new research suggests one of those inherited genetic variants is associated with a slightly shrunken brain region and lower risk of schizophrenia, according to a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences on November 16. The findings further highlight the enduring impacts of modern humans’ trysts with Neanderthals.
paras.zh: 现在，根据 11 月 16 日发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上的一项研究，新的研究表明，其中一种遗传性基因变异与大脑区域轻微萎缩和患精神分裂症的风险较低有关。这些发现进一步凸显了现代人类与尼安德特人幽会的持久影响。

paras.en: “This is a very important variant,” says Davide Marnetto, a computational biologist at the University of Turin in Italy who wasn’t involved in the research, to Michael Marshall at Nature. “Its effect is really one of the most beautiful and strong that I’ve ever seen.”
paras.zh: “这是一个非常重要的变体，”意大利都灵大学的计算生物学家达维德·马内托（Davide Marnetto）对《自然》杂志的迈克尔·马歇尔说，他没有参与这项研究。 “它的效果确实是我见过的最美丽、最强烈的效果之一。”

paras.en: Neanderthals had larger skulls than modern humans, and they were more elongated front-to-back, hinting at a different brain tissue layout. Evolutionary geneticists Hugo Zeberg and Svante Pääbo, of the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Germany, suspected the occipital lobe—which sits at the back of the brain and processes visual information—had something to do with that distinct shape.
paras.zh: 尼安德特人的头骨比现代人类更大，而且从前到后也更长，这暗示着不同的脑组织布局。德国马克斯·普朗克进化人类学研究所的进化遗传学家 Hugo Zeberg 和 Svante Pääbo 怀疑枕叶（位于大脑后部并处理视觉信息）与这种独特的形状有关。

paras.en: So, the research duo investigated gene variants known to affect occipital lobe size in people of European descent, whose DNA typically contains around 1 to 2 percent Neanderthal ancestry. Then, they looked at which variants were not present in people of sub-Saharan African descent, who have little to no Neanderthal DNA because their ancestors didn’t mingle with the extinct hominins, which evolved in Europe and Asia.
paras.zh: 因此，研究人员研究了已知影响欧洲后裔枕叶大小的基因变异，这些人的 DNA 通常含有约 1% 至 2% 的尼安德特人血统。然后，他们研究了撒哈拉以南非洲人后裔中不存在哪些变异，这些人几乎没有尼安德特人 DNA，因为他们的祖先没有与在欧洲和亚洲进化的已灭绝的古人类混在一起。

paras.en: The work revealed a genetic variant that affects the DAAM1 gene, which is linked to brain development. This variant upstream of DAAM1 was seen in all five available genomes—complete sets of genetic instructions—from Neanderthals, the team found. Importantly, it wasn’t present in the two tested genomes from Denisovans, another extinct cousin that interbred with humans. The scientists estimate that about 20 percent of people of European descent carry at least one copy of the variant, reports Science’s Michael Price.
paras.zh: 这项工作揭示了一种影响 DAAM1 基因的遗传变异，该基因与大脑发育有关。研究小组发现，DAAM1 上游的这种变异存在于尼安德特人的所有五个可用基因组（完整的遗传指令集）中。重要的是，它并不存在于丹尼索瓦人的两个测试基因组中，丹尼索瓦人是另一种与人类杂交的灭绝表亲。据《科学》杂志的迈克尔·普莱斯报道，科学家们估计，大约 20% 的欧洲人后裔至少携带一份该变体副本。

paras.en: Using data from the U.K. Biobank, which contains genetic information from about half a million participants, the team examined how the Neanderthal gene variant affects people today. Analyses revealed that having one copy—inherited from one parent—is associated with a 0.85-cubic-centimeter reduction in occipital lobe volume, whereas inheriting it from both parents doubles the shrinkage. That seems a bit surprising since Neanderthals are thought to have had bigger brains than Homo sapiens.
paras.zh: 英国生物银行包含约 50 万参与者的遗传信息，研究小组利用该数据研究了尼安德特人基因变异对当今人类的影响。分析显示，从父母一方继承的枕叶体积会减少 0.85 立方厘米，而从父母双方继承的枕叶体积会缩小一倍。这似乎有点令人惊讶，因为人们认为尼安德特人的大脑比智人更大。

paras.en: “It sounds paradoxical, but it probably is not unexpected,” since traits like brain size are influenced by hundreds, or even thousands, of genes, says Joshua Akey, a geneticist at Princeton University who wasn’t involved in the work, to Nature. “Neanderthals could have an overall larger occipital lobe, but they still contain some variants that contribute smaller sizes and some that contribute larger sizes,” he explains, and Homo sapiens may have inherited a variant that contributes to a smaller size.
paras.zh: 普林斯顿大学遗传学家约书亚·阿基（Joshua Akey）对《自然》杂志表示：“这听起来很矛盾，但可能并不意外，”因为大脑大小等特征受到数百甚至数千个基因的影响。他解释说：“尼安德特人的枕叶整体可能更大，但它们仍然包含一些导致尺寸较小的变体和一些导致尺寸较大的变体，”而智人可能继承了一种导致尺寸较小的变体。

paras.en: Having two copies of the Neanderthal variant was also associated with a nearly 10 percent reduction in schizophrenia risk, though the exact mechanism behind that effect is unclear. Future research in animals or brain organoids could provide more information, Zeberg tells Science, “but the honest answer is we don’t understand the exact mechanics at this point.”
paras.zh: 拥有两个尼安德特人变体拷贝也与精神分裂症风险降低近 10% 相关，尽管这种效应背后的确切机制尚不清楚。泽伯格告诉《科学》杂志，未来对动物或大脑类器官的研究可以提供更多信息，“但诚实的答案是，我们目前还不了解确切的机制。”

paras.en: Still, the findings align with research by Karen Berman, a neuroscientist at the National Institute of Mental Health, and colleagues, who reported in 2021 that people with more Neanderthal ancestry have lower rates of schizophrenia. The new study helps scientists further “understand the repercussions of the echoes of this genetic material in our present genetic underpinnings,” she tells the outlet.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，这些发现与美国国家心理健康研究所神经科学家 Karen Berman 及其同事的研究结果一致，他们在 2021 年报告称，尼安德特人血统较多的人患精神分裂症的几率较低。她告诉媒体，这项新研究帮助科学家进一步“了解这种遗传物质的回声对我们目前遗传基础的影响”。

paras.en: Additionally, Zeberg and Pääbo examined the variant’s potential associations with intelligence, bipolar disorder, depression, ADHD and autism spectrum disorder. They found no link between these traits and the fragment of Neanderthal DNA, and they note that their findings suggest that the size of a brain region shouldn’t be equated with cognitive abilities.
paras.zh: 此外，Zeberg 和 Pääbo 研究了该变异与智力、双相情感障碍、抑郁症、多动症和自闭症谱系障碍的潜在关联。他们发现这些特征与尼安德特人 DNA 片段之间没有联系，他们指出，他们的发现表明大脑区域的大小不应等同于认知能力。

paras.en: The researchers are now continuing to sift through data to better understand Neanderthals’ fingerprints on modern humans’ genetic makeup, and they hope to turn up additional exciting discoveries.
paras.zh: 研究人员现在正在继续筛选数据，以更好地了解尼安德特人对现代人类基因构成的指纹，他们希望能有更多令人兴奋的发现。

paras.en: “You might hear from us again,” Zeberg tells Jackie Flynn Mogensen at Scientific American.
paras.zh: “你可能会再次收到我们的消息，”泽伯格告诉《科学美国人》的杰基·弗林·摩根森。

articles.title: A Modern Forensic Investigation Reveals the Cause of Death of a 2,000-Year-Old Body Found in a Bog in Northern Ireland

paras.en: After more than 2,000 years, authorities Northern Ireland are making major discoveries in gruesome cold case. A public inquest-style inquiry has determined the cause of death of an young woman from the Iron Age, whose body was recovered in a peat bog in 2023. A coroner’s investigation concluded that she was deliberately beheaded from behind with a bladed weapon.
paras.zh: 两千多年过去了，北爱尔兰当局在这起可怕的悬案中取得了重大发现。一场公开调查式的调查确定了一名铁器时代年轻女性的死因，她的尸体于 2023 年在泥炭沼泽中被发现。验尸官的调查得出的结论是，她是被一把带刃武器故意从后面斩首的。

paras.en: Hosted at the Ulster Museum in Belfast, the proceeding synthesized findings from an international research consortium led by National Museums NI (NMNI). Although not a formal legal inquest, the hearing applied contemporary investigative standards to examine the evidence behind a death more than 20 centuries ago.
paras.zh: 该会议在贝尔法斯特的阿尔斯特博物馆举行，会议综合了由北爱尔兰国家博物馆 (NMNI) 领导的国际研究联盟的研究结果。虽然不是正式的法律调查，但听证会采用了当代调查标准来审查 20 多世纪前死亡背后的证据。

paras.en: “Finds like this that are women are incredibly rare,” Hannah Crowdy, head of curatorial at NMNI, tells the BBC’s Eve Rosato. “She’s the first of her kind in Northern Ireland at all. This helps us piece together a part of history that is quite mysterious. To honor her, it’s important to tell her story and bring that to the fore.”
paras.zh: “像这样的女性发现极其罕见，”NMNI 策展人汉娜·克劳迪 (Hannah Crowdy) 告诉 BBC 的伊芙·罗萨托 (Eve Rosato)。 “她是北爱尔兰的第一个同类。这有助于我们拼凑出一段相当神秘的历史。为了纪念她，重要的是讲述她的故事并将其带到人们的面前。”

paras.en: The remains were unearthed in October 2023, when peat workers from Bulrush Horticulture uncovered human bones in Ballymacombs More outside Bellaghy in County Londonderry.
paras.zh: 这些遗骸于 2023 年 10 月出土，当时 Bulrush Horticulture 的泥炭工人在伦敦德里郡贝拉吉郊外的 Ballymacombs More 发现了人类骨头。

paras.en: Subsequent excavations recovered further skeletal remains and a woven artifact, though no skull was found. Researchers initially thought the body was male and dubbed the individual “Bellaghy Boy,” before forensic testing revealed the remains belonged to a young woman between 15 and 22 years old. She was subsequently renamed the Ballymacombs More Woman.
paras.zh: 随后的挖掘发现了更多的骨骼遗骸和编织物，但没有发现头骨。研究人员最初认为这具尸体是男性，并称其为“贝拉吉男孩”，后来法医检测显示，尸体属于一名 15 至 22 岁的年轻女性。她随后被更名为“巴利马库姆斯更多女人”。

paras.en: Using micro-CT scanning, digital mapping, 3D imaging and targeted analyses of preserved bone, hair, skin, nails and the woven textile, researchers from nine institutions gathered clues about her diet, health and physical appearance.
paras.zh: 来自九家机构的研究人员利用微型 CT 扫描、数字测绘、3D 成像以及对保存的骨骼、头发、皮肤、指甲和机织纺织品进行有针对性的分析，收集了有关她的饮食、健康和外貌的线索。

paras.en: Cut marks on the woman’s neck appear to indicate that she was “intentionally decapitated in the bog,” Niamh Baker, NMNI’s curator of archaeology, tells the BBC.
paras.zh: NMNI 考古学馆长尼亚姆·贝克 (Niamh Baker) 告诉 BBC，这名女子脖子上的割痕似乎表明她“在沼泽中被故意斩首”。

paras.en: The reason for this decapitation is unknown. “It may be that she falls into a pattern of ritual and sacrifice that took place across northwest Europe in the Iron Age period,” Baker explains, adding that comparable Iron Age male remains found in the Republic of Ireland have been linked to leadership positions.
paras.zh: 这次斩首的原因尚不清楚。贝克解释说：“她可能陷入了铁器时代欧洲西北部发生的一种仪式和牺牲模式。”他补充说，在爱尔兰共和国发现的类似铁器时代男性遗骸与领导职位有关。

paras.en: “Was she a female sovereign?” Baker asks. “Or it may be that it was related to an agricultural or weather issue at the time.”
paras.zh: “她是女皇吗？”贝克问道。 “或者可能与当时的农业或天气问题有关。”

paras.en: “The purpose of the exercise is not to impose modern legal conclusions upon the distant past, but to provide a framework through which the available evidence could be assessed and the story of a previously unknown young woman could be told,” Joe McCrisken, the coroner who chaired the investigation, said at the inquest, the Guardian’s Rory Carroll reports.
paras.zh: 据《卫报》的罗里·卡罗尔报道，主持此次调查的验尸官乔·麦克克里斯肯 (Joe McCrisken) 在审讯中表示：“这次演习的目的不是将现代法律结论强加于遥远的过去，而是提供一个框架，通过该框架可以评估现有证据，并讲述一名以前不为人知的年轻女性的故事。”

paras.en: The Ballymacombs More Woman joins internationally famous bog bodies—including Denmark’s Tollund Man and Grauballe Man, as well as Ireland’s Clonycavan Man and Old Croghan Man—in offering rare insights into ancient societies.
paras.zh: Ballymacombs More Woman 与国际著名的沼泽组织（包括丹麦的托伦德人和格劳巴勒人，以及爱尔兰的克隆卡文人和老克罗根人）一起，为古代社会提供了罕见的见解。

paras.en: Bog discoveries inspired poems by the late Irish Nobel laureate Seamus Heaney, including “The Grauballe Man,” “The Tollund Man” and “The Tollund Man in Springtime.”
paras.zh: 沼泽的发现启发了已故爱尔兰诺贝尔奖得主谢默斯·希尼 (Seamus Heaney) 的诗歌，包括《格劳巴勒人》、《托伦德人》和《春天的托伦德人》。

paras.en: Residents of Bellaghy have embraced the young woman as one of their own, naming her Áine after an Irish goddess.
paras.zh: 贝拉吉的居民将这位年轻女子视为自己的一员，并以爱尔兰女神的名字为她命名为 Áine。

paras.en: “We feel that Áine is one of our own,” Séamus Mac an Fhirléighinn of the Bellaghy Historical Society tells the BBC. “This is her inquest, she needed her people, her family there with her to act on her behalf as advocates.”
paras.zh: “我们觉得 Áine 是我们中的一员，”贝拉吉历史学会的 Séamus Mac 和 Fhirléighinn 告诉 BBC。 “这是她的调查，她需要她的人民、她的家人和她一起代表她作为倡导者。”

paras.en: As the Ulster Museum prepares updates to its Early Peoples gallery, curators have decided not to display Ballymacombs More Woman’s physical remains, opting instead to evoke her life through mediums such as illustration and poetry, for example.
paras.zh: 当阿尔斯特博物馆准备更新其早期人民画廊时，策展人决定不展示 Ballymacombs More Woman 的遗骸，而是选择通过插图和诗歌等媒介来唤起她的生活。

paras.en: “Ballymacombs More Woman was once a person, just like us,” Crowdy says in a statement. “While the circumstances of her life and death belong to the past, her discovery raises questions that remain relevant to the future, not least the presence and care of human remains in museum collections today.”
paras.zh: “女人曾经也是一个人，就像我们一样，”克劳迪在一份声明中说。 “虽然她的生与死的情况属于过去，但她的发现提出了与未来仍然相关的问题，尤其是今天博物馆收藏中人类遗骸的存在和护理。”

articles.title: Best Early Black Friday Phone Deals (2026)
articles.author: Simon Hill

paras.en: We see tempting Black Friday phone deals every year, and in 2026, the sales have kicked off early. I spotted phones we have tested and already recommend at a cheaper price than usually, and collected them below. It’s possible some of these prices will dip lower as day-of Black Friday deals, and more phones will definitely be on sale for the event, but we’ll update this guide as we spot them.

A lovely 6.5-inch OLED screen and excellent performance, courtesy of Apple’s A19 Pro chipset, are wrapped up in a body that’s just 5.6 millimeters thick and only weighs 165 grams. Battery life isn’t stellar, and the main camera is a lone 48-MP shooter, but it’s so thin. Discounts on iPhones can be hard to find, so if you’ve had your eye on the iPhone Air, this deal is worth grabbing.
paras.zh: iPhone Air 以其超薄的外形给我们留下了深刻的印象。可爱的 6.5 英寸 OLED 屏幕和卓越的性能，得益于苹果的 A19 Pro 芯片组，机身厚度仅为 5.6 毫米，重量仅为 165 克。电池寿命不是很长，主摄像头是一个单独的 48MP 射手，但它太薄了。 iPhone 的折扣很难找到，所以如果您关注 iPhone Air，那么这笔交易值得抓住。

paras.en: Our top pick of the best folding phones pulls all of Samsung’s experience together into a fresh form factor that feels just right. The 5.5-inch cover screen is usable, and the 7.7-inch inner screen is perfect for opening two apps side by side. This is also a powerful phone with a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset and has plenty of stamina thanks to the 4,800-mAh silicon-carbon battery. paras.en: If you prefer a compact flip phone, the Samsung Galaxy Z Flip8 is calling. Samsung’s eighth-generation clamshell is wonderfully refined, slimmer than ever, and offers a 4.1-inch AMOLED cover screen with a 6.9-inch display inside. Performance and battery life are excellent. The camera will be enough for most folks, and there’s a healthy dose of AI. Best of all, this discount deletes the annual $100 price bump and knocks another $100 off. It has never been cheaper.
paras.zh: 如果您更喜欢紧凑型翻盖手机，那么三星 Galaxy Z Flip8 就是您的最佳选择。三星的第八代翻盖非常精致，比以往任何时候都更纤薄，并提供 4.1 英寸 AMOLED 盖屏，内部显示屏为 6.9 英寸。性能和电池寿命都非常出色。对于大多数人来说，相机已经足够了，而且还有适量的人工智能。最重要的是，此折扣消除了每年 100 美元的价格上涨，并再减价 100 美元。从来没有这么便宜过。

paras.en: Samsung’s most powerful phone is the pick for professionals. It combines excellent performance, great battery life, and a reliable quad-camera system. The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra has a special Privacy Display to keep folks from peeking over your shoulder at what’s on your screen. The Ultra is also the only Samsung phone with the integrated S Pen stylus. It has dipped as low as $950 before (and may do again), but this is a decent discount.

articles.title: The ‘GTA 6’ Work Blackout Is Here
articles.author: Miles Klee

paras.en: Somewhere out there, right at this moment, a couple is probably still negotiating the final terms of a contract that permits one partner to play Grand Theft Auto VI around the clock for an entire week following its Thursday release. Adults who grew up on the felony-based video game franchise are taking steps to secure sick days—and some, no doubt, are granting their own kids permission to stay home from school (despite warnings from their teachers). Streamers on Twitch and YouTube stand ready to conquer the enhanced and expanded virtual domain of Vice City, seeking out every last Easter egg.
paras.zh: 此时此刻，一对夫妇可能仍在就一份合同的最终条款进行谈判，该合同允许其中一方在《侠盗猎车手 6》周四发布后的整整一周内全天候畅玩。在基于重罪的电子游戏系列中长大的成年人正在采取措施确保病假——毫无疑问，有些人允许自己的孩子呆在家里不上学（尽管有老师的警告）。 Twitch 和 YouTube 上的主播已准备好征服罪恶都市的增强和扩展的虚拟领域，寻找每一个复活节彩蛋。

paras.en: So don’t be surprised if a console owner in your life is curiously unavailable between now and Thanksgiving. The 13-year-wait for this latest installment of the series has felt interminable enough to inspire a meme used in reaction to any surprising or unprecedented news: “We got [fill in the blank] before GTA VI.”
paras.zh: 因此，如果您生活中的某个游戏机所有者从现在到感恩节期间奇怪地无法使用，请不要感到惊讶。该系列最新作的 13 年等待让人感觉无休无止，足以激发人们对任何令人惊讶或史无前例的消息做出反应的表情包：“我们在 GTA VI 之前就得到了[填空]。”

paras.en: Especially within the tech and gaming industries, the expectation is that many developers won’t be clocking in on Thursday or Friday. (GTA VI officially launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S at midnight local time on Thursday, November 19, according to publisher Rockstar Games.)
paras.zh: 特别是在科技和游戏行业，预计许多开发人员不会在周四或周五上班。 （据发行商 Rockstar Games 称，GTA VI 于当地时间 11 月 19 日星期四午夜正式在 PlayStation 5 和 Xbox Series X|S 上发布。）

paras.en: “I’m not going to question whether folks are really sick on their sick days or how they spend a vacation day,” says Mike, an executive of a gaming studio with more than a thousand employees, who requested a pseudonym to avoid damaging professional relationships within the industry. “I want them to spend time engaging with the medium we love, and there’s no question that playing lots of video games helps you make video games.”
paras.zh: “我不会质疑人们在病假期间是否真的生病了，或者他们如何度过假期，”迈克说，他是一家拥有 1000 多名员工的游戏工作室的高管，他要求使用化名，以避免损害行业内的专业关系。 “I want them to spend time engaging with the medium we love, and there’s no question that playing lots of video games helps you make video games.”

paras.en: In October, the HR software company BambooHR concluded through data analysis and a survey of salaried workers that the PTO request rate for November 19 is nearly 13 percent higher than equivalent days in past years, while Xbox is running a promotional campaign in which gamers can generate notes from a Dr. Xbox (DJ Khaled in glasses and a lab coat) claiming that they have a “Vitamin G” deficiency and are unable to work.
paras.zh: 10 月，人力资源软件公司 BambooHR 通过数据分析和对领薪员工的调查得出结论：11 月 19 日的带薪休假申请率比往年同等日期高出近 13%。与此同时，Xbox 正在开展一场促销活动，玩家可以从 Dr. Xbox（戴着眼镜、身穿白大褂的 DJ Khaled）那里获得诊断证明，声称他们缺乏“维生素 G”，因此无法工作。

paras.en: A few companies are getting ahead of the productivity slump; the hardware and software manufacturer Logitech, for example, announced earlier this month that all 7,000 employees would be granted a paid day off for gaming, to be scheduled any time within a year or so. In announcing the policy, the company cited internal studies on the ways that gaming may potentially improve job performance and mental health.
paras.zh: 一些公司在生产力下滑之前就已经采取了行动。 the hardware and software manufacturer Logitech, for example, announced earlier this month that all 7,000 employees would be granted a paid day off for gaming, to be scheduled any time within a year or so.在宣布该政策时，该公司引用了关于游戏可能改善工作绩效和心理健康的内部研究。

paras.en: Riot Games, the publisher behind League of Legends and Valorant, has likewise made arrangements for the blockbuster event. “We have an open PTO policy, and we’ve seen leaders encourage their teams to enjoy the first day of release,” Joe Hixson, Riot Games vice president of communications, tells WIRED. “On our main campus, we'll be celebrating with a special-themed lunch menu and snacks that pay homage to the game. We also expect to see people firing it up in our console rooms during breaks and after hours.”
paras.zh: 《英雄联盟》和《Valorant》的发行商 Riot Games 也为这场轰动一时的活动做出了同样的安排。 “We have an open PTO policy, and we’ve seen leaders encourage their teams to enjoy the first day of release,” Joe Hixson, Riot Games vice president of communications, tells WIRED. “On our main campus, we'll be celebrating with a special-themed lunch menu and snacks that pay homage to the game. We also expect to see people firing it up in our console rooms during breaks and after hours.”

paras.en: Riot additionally offers the Play Fund, a stipend of $25 a month for employees to spend on gaming titles across platforms and genres. “It makes us better developers by deepening our understanding of what makes a great player experience,” Hixson says.
paras.zh: Riot 还提供“游戏基金”，每月向员工发放 25 美元的津贴，供其用于购买跨平台、跨类型的游戏。Hixson表示：“通过加深我们对什么是出色玩家体验的理解，这使我们成为更好的开发者。”

paras.en: Mike tells WIRED that on in-office workdays, the company has a typical absentee rate of 5 to 7 percent due to vacations, illness, travel, and the like. He estimates that on Thursday, it will be more like 10 or 12 percent. “Now, on the Friday, will there be some number of employees who are ‘working’ when they’re at home but also suspiciously slow to answer messages while they have big chunks of their calendar blocked out for ‘deep individual work?’” says the studio leader. “Yeah, probably.”
paras.zh: Mike tells WIRED that on in-office workdays, the company has a typical absentee rate of 5 to 7 percent due to vacations, illness, travel, and the like.他估计周四这一数字将更接近 10% 或 12%。 “Now, on the Friday, will there be some number of employees who are ‘working’ when they’re at home but also suspiciously slow to answer messages while they have big chunks of their calendar blocked out for ‘deep individual work?’” says the studio leader. “是的，可能是。”

paras.en: But it’s hardly unusual in the business for people to select their days off to accommodate a major game release, Mike says. In 2023, he was out for three days to play The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, which he recalls as “paradise.”
paras.zh: 但迈克表示，人们选择休息日以适应大型游戏的发布，这在业内并不罕见。 2023 年，他为了玩《塞尔达传说：王国之泪》而缺席了三天，他回忆说那是“天堂”。

paras.en: That said, he notes that the next leap forward for GTA is no ordinary affair. The hype for this franchise, he explains, “breaks containment,” reaching people who have not bought a new title in years.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，他指出《GTA》的下一次飞跃并不是一件平常的事情。他解释说，对这个系列的炒作“打破了遏制”，吸引了多年来没有购买新游戏的人们。

paras.en: That’s why even companies without ties to gaming culture have been making allowances for so-called Grand Theft Auto Flu. On Monday, the social team for the luxury real estate firm Serhant posted a video of CEO Ryan Serhant (also the host of the Netflix reality show Owning Manhattan) agreeing with an employee that if the clip garnered 400,000 likes, the office would close for GTA day. “You’ll never get that,” Serhant predicted.
paras.zh: 这就是为什么即使是与游戏文化无关的公司也一直在考虑所谓的侠盗猎车手流感。周一，豪华房地产公司 Serhant 的社交团队发布了一段视频，首席执行官 Ryan Serhant（也是 Netflix 真人秀《拥有曼哈顿》的主持人）与一名员工达成一致，如果该视频获得 40 万个赞，办公室将在 GTA 日关闭。 “你永远不会明白这一点，”瑟汉特预测道。

paras.en: The post picked up 1.4 million likes within 24 hours, prompting an update on Tuesday: The firm would honor Serhant’s promise. “We are big supporters of our team, their passions both in and out of real estate, and all things culture and tech,” Serhant said in a statement to WIRED, noting that “13 years of anticipation deserves a day off.” The company announced a floating holiday to staff on Wednesday, to be used any time before the end of 2026.
paras.zh: 这篇帖子在 24 小时内获得了 140 万个赞，促使周二更新：该公司将兑现 Serhant 的承诺。 Serhant 在给《连线》的一份声明中表示：“我们是我们团队的大力支持者，他们对房地产内外以及所有文化和科技领域都充满热情。”他指出，“13 年的期待值得休息一天。”该公司周三向员工宣布了浮动假期，可在 2026 年底前的任何时间使用。

paras.en: Also on Wednesday, Arizona Beverages announced a sweepstakes for social media followers who may have felt they couldn’t afford to miss a work shift. Dropping a PTO request for GTA day in the comment section, the company said, would enter that person for a chance to win $500 to cover their lost hours.
paras.zh: 同样在周三，亚利桑那饮料公司宣布为社交媒体粉丝举办抽奖活动，这些粉丝可能觉得自己不能错过轮班。该公司表示，如果在评论部分放弃 PTO 的 GTA 日请求，则该人将有机会赢得 500 美元，以弥补他们损失的时间。

paras.en: With this level of fanfare, nearly 16 million preorders bringing in revenue of $1.5 billion, and expectations of 45 million sales in its launch quarter, GTA VI is poised to be the most significant entertainment event of the year and the biggest video game of all time. It’s little wonder, then, that some have warned about the global economy slowing down this week as fans ignore their email inboxes and Slack messages to indulge in some extended role-play as streetwise criminals. One economist has estimated that the GTA release could cost the US economy $1 billion in lost productivity.
paras.zh: 凭借如此高的宣传力度、近 1600 万份预订带来 15 亿美元的收入，以及发布季度 4500 万份的销量预期，GTA VI 有望成为今年最重要的娱乐活动和有史以来最大的视频游戏。因此，难怪一些人警告本周全球经济放缓，因为粉丝们忽视了他们的电子邮件收件箱和 Slack 消息，沉迷于街头犯罪分子的长期角色扮演。一位经济学家估计，GTA 的发布可能会给美国经济造成 10 亿美元的生产力损失。

paras.en: Mike isn’t buying this, however, arguing that the hype about “how GTA will impact the GDP or cause a failure of the power grid or whatever are just silly.” He points out that “PC is the biggest individual platform, and the PC launch timing is still unclear.” Neither have Rockstar and Take-Two announced a launch date for the game’s online multiplayer mode; only the single-player experience will be available on Thursday.
paras.zh: 然而，迈克并不相信这一点，他认为有关“GTA 将如何影响 GDP 或导致电网故障或其他任何事情”的炒作都是愚蠢的。他指出，“PC是最大的个人平台，PC的推出时间仍不清楚。” Rockstar 和 Take-Two 都没有宣布游戏在线多人模式的发布日期；周四仅提供单人游戏体验。

paras.en: Andy Garin, an associate professor of economics at Carnegie Mellon University, also finds the concerns about sluggish market activity to be overblown.
paras.zh: 卡内基梅隆大学经济学副教授安迪·加林也认为，对市场活动低迷的担忧有些言过其实。

paras.en: “Speculation about a hit to productivity around these kinds of events pops up a lot, particularly during the Olympics or World Cup, when time zone differences mean major events are during the workday,” Garin says. “I don't think the release date of GTA VI will be that different than these sort of events that happen all the time, particularly if workers are using their allotted PTO or scheduling flexibility baked into their jobs.”
paras.zh: 加林说：“关于这类活动对生产力造成影响的猜测经常出现，特别是在奥运会或世界杯期间，时区差异意味着重大活动都在工作日进行。” “我认为 GTA VI 的发布日期不会与经常发生的此类事件有什么不同，特别是如果工人正在使用分配的 PTO 或工作安排的灵活性。”

paras.en: Malcolm Robinson, who has a YouTube channel dedicated to gaming and works at a veterans hospital, tells WIRED that the GTA release just happens to fall on his day off. “I plan on playing it for about eight to 12 hours straight on the first night,” he says.
paras.zh: 马尔科姆·罗宾逊 (Malcolm Robinson) 在一家退伍军人医院工作，拥有一个专门负责游戏的 YouTube 频道，他告诉《连线》杂志，《侠盗猎车手》的发布恰逢他休息日。 “我计划在第一晚连续玩大约 8 到 12 个小时，”他说。

paras.en: Others have had no difficulty setting that time aside. One redditor who works as the distribution coordinator for a chain of auto shops in Colorado and requested anonymity out of concern for professional consequences says that he would have called in sick on Thursday but had the option to use PTO. His supervisor asked if it was to play GTA, which he confirmed. “He was like, ‘I get it, enjoy,’” this gamer reports. He plans to play along with his girlfriend, who is also taking the day off, and is excited to “sink my teeth into it before the entire thing gets spoiled.”
paras.zh: 其他人则毫不费力地把这段时间放在一边。一位在科罗拉多州一家连锁汽车商店担任分销协调员的 Reddit 用户出于对职业后果的担忧而要求匿名，他表示他本来会在周四请病假，但可以选择使用 PTO。他的主管询问是否要玩 GTA，他确认了这一点。 “他说，‘我明白了，享受吧，’”这位玩家说道。他计划和女友一起玩，女友也请了一天假，他很兴奋“在整个事情被破坏之前全力以赴”。

paras.en: James Lord, a data entry coordinator in Edmonton, Alberta, tells WIRED that he initially offered to let his team take Thursday off for GTA purposes. When none of them expressed interest in the game, he says, he “jumped at the opportunity” to claim the day for himself. He’s been playing Grand Theft Auto since the original top-down POV game for the PC came out in the late 1990s.
paras.zh: 阿尔伯塔省埃德蒙顿的数据录入协调员詹姆斯·洛德 (James Lord) 告诉《连线》杂志，他最初提出让他的团队在星期四休假，以处理 GTA 的问题。他说，当他们没有人对这款游戏表现出兴趣时，他“抓住了这个机会”，为自己赢得了这一天。自 20 世纪 90 年代末 PC 版自上而下的第一人称视角游戏问世以来，他就一直在玩《侠盗猎车手》。

paras.en: Lord, too, is wary of spoilers—he locked down his social media on Tuesday night to avoid any—but nostalgia and lifelong relationships are even better reasons to jump into GTA VI as soon as he can. He’s going to boot up the game while on a call with his brother, who lives across the country, and they’ll be joined by friends living in Pennsylvania and Texas. It’s a reunion experience that wouldn’t be possible without a break from the 9-to-5 job.
paras.zh: 洛德也对剧透持谨慎态度——他在周二晚上锁定了自己的社交媒体以避免剧透——但怀旧和终生的关系是他尽快进入 GTA VI 的更好理由。他将在与居住在全国各地的兄弟通话时启动游戏，居住在宾夕法尼亚州和德克萨斯州的朋友也将加入他们的行列。如果不摆脱朝九晚五的工作，这种团聚体验是不可能实现的。

paras.en: “We lead busy lives now,” Lord reflects, “so having to set time aside for the game of the decade is important to us.”
paras.zh: “我们现在过着忙碌的生活，”洛德反思道，“所以必须为这十年的比赛留出时间对我们来说很重要。”

articles.title: Australia’s Plan to Manage Neil the Unruly Seal Involves ‘Hazing’ and ‘Seal Enrichment’
articles.author: Tess Owen

paras.en: There is a six-year-old elephant seal in Tasmania named Neil who has a taste for light property damage during the winter months. Now, the state has a management plan.
paras.zh: 塔斯马尼亚有一只名叫尼尔的六岁象海豹，它喜欢在冬季遭受轻微的财产损失。现在，国家有一个管理计划。

paras.en: Neil's annual “hauling out” and subsequent misadventures on the southeastern part of the island has delighted locals, making him a local mascot and a viral social media star.
paras.zh: 尼尔一年一度的“出逃”以及随后在岛东南部发生的不幸事件让当地人感到高兴，使他成为当地的吉祥物和社交媒体上的明星。

paras.en: But Neil’s on-land hijinks—as he experiences his yearly “catastrophic molt,” during which he, like all elephant seals, sheds and replaces his top level of fur and epidermis— has also created headaches for local officials. Neil, who weighs over 2,000 pounds, has destroyed walkways, flattened bollards, bowled through fences, and rammed vehicles. The enormous and growing public interest in Neil has also been a source of concern, as officials spend tens of thousands of Australian dollars to keep the public at a safe distance from him.
paras.zh: 但尼尔在陆地上的狂欢——他经历了每年一次的“灾难性换毛”，在此期间，他像所有象海豹一样，脱落并更换了他的顶层皮毛和表皮——也让当地官员感到头疼。尼尔体重超过 2000 磅，他毁坏了人行道、压扁了护柱、撞穿了栅栏、撞坏了车辆。公众对尼尔的巨大且不断增长的兴趣也引起了人们的担忧，因为官员们花费了数万澳元来让公众与他保持安全距离。

paras.en: The Tasmanian government, finding itself in a precarious position, has finally decided to take action. The Department of Natural Resources and Environment published a 27-page dossier this week titled “Neil the Seal Management Plan.”
paras.zh: 塔斯马尼亚政府发现自己处境岌岌可危，最终决定采取行动。自然资源和环境部本周发布了一份长达 27 页的档案，题为“尼尔海豹管理计划”。

paras.en: “The purpose of this Plan is to set out a framework for managing the resident elephant seal known as Neil in Tasmania, recognising the complex challenges associated with his recurring haul out period,” the dossier states.
paras.zh: 档案指出：“该计划的目的是制定一个框架来管理塔斯马尼亚岛的常驻象海豹尼尔，认识到与它反复出现的迁移期相关的复杂挑战。”

paras.en: Neil has a dedicated task force to monitor his whereabouts and according to the dossier, they would take a “non-intervention,” hands-off approach if he hauls out in a secluded location. They’d keep tabs on Neil from a distance, erecting signs around the area to alert the public of Neil’s presence while advising them to keep their distance. Should the public tempt fate and approach Neil, the task force can call in security personnel to keep people and the seal safe.
paras.zh: 尼尔有一个专门的工作组来监视他的行踪，根据档案，如果他在一个僻静的地方被拖出来，他们将采取“不干预”、不干涉的方式。他们会从远处监视尼尔，在该地区周围竖起标志，提醒公众尼尔的存在，同时建议他们保持距离。如果公众冒险接近尼尔，特别工作组可以召集安全人员来保证人员和海豹的安全。

paras.en: The second contingency plan is titled “on-site seal management,” which would be necessary if Neil comes ashore in a more public location, and has immediate access to roads and critical infrastructure that up the odds of molting-induced mayhem. One proposed management option involves “hazing,” which would essentially treat Neil like a frat pledge. The dossier doesn’t get into specifics—ostensibly there’s no paddling or eating a live goldfish involved—but highlights what it calls a “non-violent method of using deterrents and negative associations to disturb an animal, compelling them to move,” which can include “controlled visual, tactile and vocal stimuli where appropriate.”
paras.zh: 第二个应急计划的标题是“现场海豹管理”，如果尼尔在一个更公共的地方上岸，并且可以立即进入道路和关键基础设施，这将是必要的，这会增加蜕皮引起的混乱的可能性。一项拟议的管理方案涉及“欺辱”，这基本上将尼尔视为兄弟会的誓言。该档案没有详细说明——表面上没有涉及划动或吃活金鱼——但强调了所谓的“使用威慑和负面联想来扰乱动物、迫使它们移动的非暴力方法”，其中可以包括“在适当的情况下控制视觉、触觉和声音刺激”。

paras.en: The document also notes that Neil appears to be adapting to and thus eluding “standard management practices,” meaning that the task force needs to stay nimble in coming up with new methods to curb Neil’s taste for antics.
paras.zh: 该文件还指出，尼尔似乎正在适应并因此逃避“标准管理实践”，这意味着工作组需要保持灵活，想出新方法来遏制尼尔的滑稽动作。

paras.en: Tasmanian officials also propose “seal enrichment,” which they say would be used in tandem with other management options, to redirect “natural exploratory behaviors” (like engaging with infrastructure) towards decoy items “designed to withstand repeated interaction.”
paras.zh: 塔斯马尼亚官员还提议“海豹浓缩”，他们说这将与其他管理方案结合使用，将“自然探索行为”（例如与基础设施接触）转向“旨在承受重复互动”的诱饵项目。

paras.en: Officials also say that despite their best efforts to avoid Neil-related interruptions to daily life, “significant events,” such as road closures, public safety incidents, relocation or translocation activities, or wildlife-born diseases, are still liable to happen. During such events, members of the public are advised to contact the Marine Mammal Hotline, also known as “0427 WHALES.”
paras.zh: 官员们还表示，尽管他们尽最大努力避免与尼尔有关的日常生活中断，但“重大事件”，如道路封闭、公共安全事件、搬迁或易位活动或野生动物传播的疾病，仍然有可能发生。在此类活动期间，建议公众联系海洋哺乳动物热线，也称为“0427 WHALES”。

articles.title: Zane Lowe Talks Interviewing Stars & Growing Apple Music Radio to 50M Unique Listeners Per Month
articles.author: Kristin Robinson

paras.en: Zane Lowe has become one of the music industry’s go-to press tour stops. As global creative director at Apple Music and host of its popular Zane Lowe Show, the New Zealand-born host has become known for his conversational interview style and for being the face of the Apple Music brand.
paras.zh: 赞恩·洛 (Zane Lowe) 已成为音乐界媒体巡演的首选站之一。作为 Apple Music 的全球创意总监和热门 Zane Lowe Show 的主持人，这位出生于新西兰的主持人以其对话式采访风格和 Apple Music 品牌的代言人而闻名。

paras.en: Unlike Spotify and other competitors, Apple Music has taken an approach to editorial that’s less focused on algorithmic recommendation and playlisting and more focused on hiring radio personalities, who, like Lowe, put a face to the service’s music. While it’s now common to find artists big and small at Apple Music’s new studios in Culver City, Calif., Lowe explains that it wasn’t always this way. When he first started building the company’s voice as a destination for artist interviews, after a successful stint at BBC Radio 1, “it was kind of crickets,” he tells Billboard.
paras.zh: 与 Spotify 和其他竞争对手不同的是，Apple Music 采取的社论方式不太注重算法推荐和播放列表，而是更注重雇佣电台名人，比如 Lowe 等，他们为该服务的音乐提供了面孔。虽然现在在 Apple Music 位于加利福尼亚州卡尔弗城的新工作室中发现大大小小的艺术家很常见，但 Lowe 解释说，情况并非总是如此。在 BBC Radio 1 取得成功后，当他第一次开始将公司的声音打造为艺术家采访的目的地时，“这有点像蟋蟀，”他告诉 Billboard。

paras.en: “As upsetting as that was at the time, two good things came out of it,” he says of that time 11 years ago. “Number one, it snapped me back into the reality force field of building something from scratch, and number two, it made us focus really clearly and in a big way on new and emerging artists.” Early evangelists, like a then-teenage Billie Eilish, Khalid and Bryson Tiller, quickly grew into the industry’s future stars, and as they grew, so did Apple Music Radio.
paras.zh: “尽管当时令人沮丧，但也带来了两件好事，”他谈到 11 年前的那段时间时说道。 “第一，它让我回到了从头开始构建一些东西的现实力场，第二，它让我们非常清晰地、很大程度上关注新兴艺术家。”早期的布道者，比如当时十几岁的 Billie Eilish、Khalid 和 Bryson Tiller，很快就成长为该行业的未来之星，随着他们的成长，Apple Music Radio 也在成长。

paras.en: In the latest episode of Billboard On the Record, Lowe reveals that Apple Music Radio now reaches 50 million unique listeners every month and has played more than 6,500 this year alone — half of which Lowe describes as “new or emerging.”
paras.zh: 在最新一集的《Billboard On the Record》中，Lowe 透露，Apple Music Radio 现在每个月都有 5000 万独立听众，仅今年就播放了 6,500 多次——Lowe 称其中一半是“新的或新兴的”。

paras.en: “Think about 3,300 artists roughly getting played, who may be on their first song, their first EP, their first album,” Lowe says. “It’s proof of concept. It’s great.”
paras.zh: “想想大概有 3,300 名艺术家被演奏，他们可能会出现在他们的第一首歌、他们的第一张 EP、他们的第一张专辑中，”Lowe 说。 “这是概念验证。太棒了。”

paras.en: To watch this episode of Billboard On the Record, check out the YouTube video below or click here for more viewing and listening options. An edited and condensed excerpt of the conversation can also be found below.
paras.zh: 要观看 Billboard On the Record 的这一集，请查看下面的 YouTube 视频或单击此处获取更多观看和收听选项。下面还提供了经过编辑和浓缩的对话摘录。

paras.en: You came from the world of traditional radio. You did local interviews in New Zealand, and you also were a host at BBC Radio 1 for a long time, but a traditional radio interview is much different from what you do now on the Zane Lowe Show at Apple Music. How do you approach interviews differently depending on the format?
paras.zh: 你来自传统广播的世界。您在新西兰进行了当地采访，并且还长期担任 BBC Radio 1 的主持人，但传统的电台采访与您现在在 Apple Music 的 Zane Lowe Show 上所做的采访有很大不同。根据不同的形式，您如何以不同的方式进行采访？

paras.en: Well, [the approach has] changed a lot. New Zealand is a touring spot and a spot for artists. But back then you would get people at the end of a long run of shows or whatever, and a lot of times, press felt like an obligation rather [than something fun].
paras.zh: 嗯，[方法]发生了很大变化。新西兰是一个旅游胜地，也是艺术家的聚集地。但那时你会在长时间的演出或其他什么结束时吸引人们，很多时候，媒体感觉像是一种义务而不是[而不是有趣的事情]。

paras.en: So I had this pretty amazing kind of training ground in New Zealand, where I talked to everyone from Meat Loaf to the Beastie Boys to Smashing Pumpkins and k.d. lang and this wide variety of artists, because there wasn’t a lot of opportunity on screen to do that [locally]. That’s where I got into the idea of what interviewing could be.
paras.zh: 所以我在新西兰有一个非常令人惊奇的训练场，在那里我与从 Meat Loaf 到 Beastie Boys 到 Smashing Pumpkins 和 k.d. 的所有人进行了交谈。郎和各种各样的艺术家，因为银幕上没有太多机会这样做（本地）。这就是我开始了解面试的想法的地方。

paras.en: But to your point, on radio, which came later, you’re constantly reminded that people can turn off at any moment, and so your decision-making becomes about trying to keep people hooked into the radio experience, which goes against your instincts in conversation sometimes, because someone can say something really interesting, and you’re like, “Man, I feel like we’ve been on the air for five minutes meaning to get to a song,” and you ignore the opportunities in front of you because of all these external factors.
paras.zh: 但就你的观点而言，在后来出现的广播中，你不断地被提醒人们可以随时关闭，所以你的决策变成了试图让人们沉浸在广播体验中，这有时违背你在谈话中的本能，因为有人可能会说一些非常有趣的事情，你会说，“伙计，我觉得我们已经播出了五分钟，意思是要听一首歌”，并且由于所有这些外部因素，你忽略了面前的机会。

paras.en: There was a whole period of time when I was not in a comfortable space for interviews on radio. I was really trying to make great radio, but it was really getting on YouTube that changed that. It was my Jay-Z interview, which he insisted we make long-form and insisted we put on YouTube, that got me back to almost where I started. It was this space where conversation can run free, and you just gotta, you know, put it in front of people, and if it’s compelling, they’ll watch it. If not, they’ll move on.
paras.zh: 有一段时间我没有在一个舒适的空间接受电台采访。我真的很想制作出色的广播节目，但 YouTube 的出现确实改变了这一点。正是我对 Jay-Z 的采访，他坚持要求我们制作长篇，并坚持要求我们将其放到 YouTube 上，这让我几乎回到了起点。在这个空间里，对话可以自由进行，你只需要把它放在人们面前，如果它引人注目，他们就会观看。如果没有，他们就会继续前进。

paras.en: I think with radio you’re also reaching a group of people that probably don’t know anything about the artist, whereas now, if someone’s tuning into the Zane Lowe Show, it’s probably because they care about the artist a bit.
paras.zh: 我认为通过广播，你还可以接触到一群可能对艺术家一无所知的人，而现在，如果有人收听 Zane Lowe Show，可能是因为他们有点关心这位艺术家。

paras.en: That’s definitely something that I’ve become comfortable with: the fact that we’re probably a targeted experience. Like, yeah some people will stumble across us, whatever, and you hope that they stick around. But I’ve really been focused on artists and music fans because I’m both of those things. So anytime that I’ve ever tried to dabble in a world where those things come along for the ride into a bigger room or a bigger opportunity, it’s never really landed for me. Like, I do what I do and continue to have this really amazing journey in music and conversation, because I think that those two things kind of remind me all the time that that’s where I should be. I’m not really a hitmaker. I’m not the person that goes in front of the camera and people are like, “I love that guy. Let’s watch this at 7 p.m. on a Friday.”
paras.zh: 这绝对是我已经习惯的事情：我们可能是一种有针对性的体验。就像，是的，有些人会偶然发现我们，无论如何，你希望他们留下来。但我真的很关注艺术家和乐迷，因为我就是这两类人。因此，每当我尝试涉足一个充满这些东西的世界时，它就会进入一个更大的房间或一个更大的机会，但它从来没有真正适合我。就像，我做我所做的事情，并继续在音乐和对话中进行这段非常奇妙的旅程，因为我认为这两件事一直提醒我，那就是我应该在的地方。我并不是一个真正的热门人。我不是那种在镜头前出现的人，人们会说，“我爱那个人。我们周五晚上 7 点看这个吧。”

paras.en: I’m wondering how being a musician yourself has informed your interviews?
paras.zh: 我想知道你自己作为一名音乐家对你的采访有何影响？

paras.en: It was an arm wrestle for a long time. It was a real tug-of-war between what I felt I should be doing and what I felt that I was good at doing. I think the era and the geography of it made the idea or concept of being a successful artist who can keep the lights on by making music alone seem very challenging. New Zealand in the ’90s…I didn’t feel that there was an audience that was going to rally around it, but I knew I wanted to stay in music, and so when I got the opportunity to talk to artists, it came so naturally to me because I guess I speak that language. That’s when the sort of lane opened up, and I started to move with some purpose and some pace. It took me further away from the making of the music, and that created some real self-appointed guilt. Like, “Oh, my God, I should be back here doing that. Why am I out here doing this?”
paras.zh: 这是一场很长一段时间的扳手腕比赛。在我认为我应该做的事情和我认为我擅长做的事情之间，这是一场真正的拉锯战。我认为那个时代和地理使得成为一名成功的艺术家仅靠音乐来保持光芒的想法或概念看起来非常具有挑战性。 90 年代的新西兰……我不觉得有观众会聚集在它周围，但我知道我想留在音乐领域，所以当我有机会与艺术家交谈时，这对我来说是如此自然，因为我想我会说这种语言。就在那时，这条小路打开了，我开始带着某种目的和步伐前进。它让我远离了音乐的创作，这让我产生了一些真正的自认内疚。就像，“哦，天哪，我应该回到这里做这件事。为什么我要在这里做这件事？”

paras.en: Mike Skinner, who performs and creates as The Streets, took me aside one day and was like, “I see that you struggle with this, but just because you talk about artists doesn’t mean you aren’t one. The fact that you’re both helps us to communicate in a more comfortable and honest way, because there isn’t separation between your craft and our craft. You understand both.” That really was a big turning point for me at a moment in my life. And I kind of made peace with both of them coexisting. And ever since then, honestly, I’ve kind of let them just be really good friends, and I’ve just been unapologetic about the fact that I make music… I like that it’s both, and it definitely has helped me in times when artists have been unsure about how far they want to go into their craft.
paras.zh: 迈克·斯金纳 (Mike Skinner) 是 The Streets 的表演和创作者，有一天他把我拉到一边，说道：“我看到你对此很挣扎，但仅仅因为你谈论艺术家并不意味着你不是艺术家。事实上，你们俩都有助于我们以一种更舒适和诚实的方式进行交流，因为你的技艺和我们的技艺之间没有分离。你都了解。”这对我来说确实是人生中的一个重大转折点。我对他们两个共存感到和睦。从那时起，老实说，我就让他们成为真正的好朋友，而且我对我创作音乐的事实毫无歉意……我喜欢两者兼而有之，而且在艺术家不确定他们想在自己的技艺上走多远的时候，这确实对我有帮助。

paras.en: I really love music. It has informed and guided my entire life and continues to be there for me and help me better understand the world and myself to this day, more and more every day. And therefore, I have so much love and admiration for people that make it, because I’m drawn into that experience myself.
paras.zh: 我真的很喜欢音乐。它为我的一生提供了信息和指导，并继续陪伴着我，帮助我更好地了解世界和我自己，直到今天，每一天都越来越深入。因此，我对那些成功的人充满了爱和钦佩，因为我自己也被这种经历所吸引。

paras.en: Do you ever get jaded, being so close to the music industry?
paras.zh: 离音乐行业如此之近，你是否感到厌倦？

paras.en: Yeah, oh yeah. There are days when I just don’t understand decisions that are made, the way things — sort of the architecture of it, the imbalance of it. That stuff can keep me up at night, for real. But I never get jaded by music — listening to it, playing it — never.
paras.zh: 是啊，哦，是啊。有时候，我就是不明白所做的决定、事情的方式——它的架构、它的不平衡。这些东西真的会让我彻夜难眠。但我从来没有对音乐感到厌倦——听它、演奏它——从来没有。

paras.en: You see so many artists come through the studio and talk to you about all sorts of experiences in the music industry. What do you think you see as a common throughline in the artists that navigate the industry most successfully?
paras.zh: 你看到很多艺术家来到工作室，和你谈论音乐行业的各种经历。您认为最成功地驾驭这个行业的艺术家的共同主线是什么？

paras.en: What’s a throughline? I think having real knowledge of self — like, a real awareness of the world you want to create, what you want to make…I think the more invested you are in what you’re doing, the more successful you can be. And that is a silver lining of the last 10, 15 years in the music industry. The whole shape of it has changed.
paras.zh: 什么是贯穿线？我认为对自我有真正的了解——比如，对你想要创造的世界、你想要创造什么有真正的认识……我认为你对自己所做的事情投入越多，你就能越成功。这是过去 10、15 年音乐行业的一线希望。整个形状都变了。

paras.en: I also think you need to have a good team around you — [another] constant [throughline] is being able to choose people really carefully.
paras.zh: 我还认为你周围需要有一支优秀的团队——[另一个]不变的[贯穿线]是能够非常仔细地选择人员。

paras.en: I think about this all the time: How many artists could have made it if the circumstances were different?
paras.zh: 我一直在想：如果环境不同的话，有多少艺术家能够做到呢？

paras.en: A much longer list than the ones that did.
paras.zh: 比之前的列表要长得多。

paras.en: Some streaming services have leaned heavily into the realm of algorithmic discovery, but Apple Music has always been about its radio service and its people. I want to hear you reflect on that and why that has been the approach that Apple Music has taken, because, frankly, it could be a lot cheaper to just be like, “Let the algorithm do it.”
paras.zh: 一些流媒体服务严重依赖算法发现领域，但 Apple Music 始终关注其广播服务和员工。我想听听你对此的反思，以及为什么 Apple Music 采取了这种方法，因为，坦率地说，“让算法来做”可能会便宜得多。

paras.en: Well, we don’t want to say that too loudly, because someone could be like, “Wait a minute, we could cut costs here? Man, how did we not think of that!” Look, I mean, jokes aside, we’ve been incredibly fortunate, and I’ve been incredibly fortunate to take that step from the BBC into a company and to work with people that value exactly what it is you’re describing: this idea of place and this experience of sharing things with each other, and how meaningful it is when someone shares a record with you and it comes with context. It’s a gift…
paras.zh: 好吧，我们不想说得太大声，因为有人可能会说，“等一下，我们可以在这里削减成本？伙计，我们怎么没想到这一点！”听着，我的意思是，抛开笑话不谈，我们非常幸运，我非常幸运能够从 BBC 迈出这一步，进入一家公司，并与那些真正重视您所描述的内容的人一起工作：这种地方的想法和这种彼此分享事物的经历，以及当有人与您分享带有背景的记录时，这是多么有意义。这是一份礼物……

paras.en: [The human approach is] part of the connection that romanticizes the experience of music… When I started here at Apple Music, it was very clear that that was very important to everybody who was responsible for bringing Apple Music to life.
paras.zh: [人性化的方法是]将音乐体验浪漫化的联系的一部分……当我开始在 Apple Music 工作时，很明显，这对于每个负责将 Apple Music 变为现实的人来说都非常重要。

paras.en: I remember conversations with Jimmy Iovine, who I worked for for years, where he was like, “You need to move the needle. You need to go and find out what’s moving people, and let the tech people worry about building the tech and making the design great. You just need to get inside the conversation and the music and find out what’s great. Don’t worry about what genre it is or whether this or that is big or not. Just define what’s great.” We’ve held true to that principle all the way through. I mean, we are a very human-focused music streaming service — the most, I would say. Not trying to make a hierarchy of what’s more human than not, but we definitely are on that side of it…
paras.zh: 我记得与我共事多年的吉米·艾欧文 (Jimmy Iovine) 的谈话，他说：“你需要改变现状。你需要找出什么能打动人们，让技术人员去关心如何构建技术并让设计变得更好。你只需要深入对话和音乐，找出什么是伟大的。不要担心它是什么流派，或者这个或那个是否大。只需定义什么是伟大的。”我们自始至终都恪守这一原则。我的意思是，我们是一个非常以人为本的音乐流媒体服务——我想说的是。并不是试图建立一个人性与非人性的等级制度，但我们肯定是站在这一边的……

paras.en: I think that really does drive a lot of the decision-making, the decisions we make at Apple Music: How are we serving artists and the artistic community in a way that is of most value and of most service? They will feel heard. They will feel supported, and therefore the artists will feel like they’ve chosen the right place to come to the fans, because the artists are happy.
paras.zh: 我认为这确实推动了我们在 Apple Music 做出的很多决策：我们如何以最有价值和最具服务性的方式为艺术家和艺术社区提供服务？他们会感到被倾听。他们会感到受到支持，因此艺术家会觉得他们选择了正确的地方来接触粉丝，因为艺术家很高兴。

paras.en: I also think that makes sense for Apple as an overall brand, which is known for leaning into design and high quality. Do you see the liquid glass redesign for Apple Music as part of that too?
paras.zh: 我也认为这对于苹果作为一个整体品牌来说是有意义的，苹果以注重设计和高品质而闻名。您是否也认为 Apple Music 的液态玻璃重新设计也是其中的一部分？

paras.en: Yeah, again, that speaks to, like, the idea of, you know, art being created by human beings. You know, I can’t speak to the decision behind that, but I can definitely appreciate [it].
paras.zh: 是的，这再次说明了人类创造艺术的想法。你知道，我不能谈论这背后的决定，但我绝对可以欣赏[它]。

paras.en: We could have created that in a way that could utilize all of the tech available. We could type that into a prompt. But at the end of the day, seeing how it’s made is so much more additionally inspiring than just seeing it. It speaks to, I think, what we try to do here, which is, we love the process of what we do, and the result is a byproduct of getting to do it and loving to do it. The way it was created [was like]: Here’s Fred [Again..] — Fred has never done anything programmatic in his life. This is a guy who’s built an entire fan base and musical legacy out of doing things that are so unique every time. He’s the perfect person to create something that speaks to us from an audio standpoint. So let’s take that, create the vibration, let’s build the logo out of that. You know, if you can, why wouldn’t you?
paras.zh: 我们本可以以一种可以利用所有可用技术的方式来创建它。我们可以将其输入到提示中。但归根结底，看到它是如何制作的比仅仅看到它更鼓舞人心。我认为，这说明了我们在这里尝试做的事情，即我们热爱我们所做的事情的过程，而结果是开始做这件事并热爱做这件事的副产品。它的创建方式[就像]：这是弗雷德[再次..]——弗雷德一生中从未做过任何程序化的事情。这个人每次都做出如此独特的事情，建立了整个粉丝群和音乐遗产。他是创造从音频角度与我们对话的东西的完美人选。因此，让我们以此为基础，创造振动，并以此为基础构建徽标。你知道，如果可以，为什么不呢？

paras.en: I mean, yeah, you have the budget at Apple.
paras.zh: 我的意思是，是的，你在苹果有预算。

paras.en: You know, I get it, Apple money, but I mean, isn’t this why we make home movies? Isn’t this why we start writing songs on a Tascam four-track? Isn’t this why you make demos and do things? Because we get addicted to the process of doing it. We love to make it. That’s why I don’t understand the idea of prompt over process…I have no interest in prompting for creative results. It’s a replacement theory that leaves me completely cold at best. At worst, it keeps me up at night. It makes me furious.
paras.zh: 你知道，我明白，苹果的钱，但我的意思是，这不是我们制作家庭电影的原因吗？这不是我们开始在 Tascam 四轨上写歌的原因吗？这不是你制作演示和做事的原因吗？因为我们会对做事的过程上瘾。我们喜欢做到这一点。这就是为什么我不理解提示胜过过程的想法……我对提示创造性结果没有兴趣。这是一种替代理论，充其量也让我感到完全冷漠。最坏的情况是，它让我彻夜难眠。这让我很愤怒。

paras.en: It’s a treat to interview an interviewer. I’m wondering how you approach an interview when the artist shows up and they are not their best — they’re tired, they’re hungover. Whatever. How do you try to build rapport with them?
paras.zh: 采访面试官是一种享受。我想知道当艺术家出现并且他们没有达到最佳状态时你如何接受采访——他们累了，他们宿醉了。任何。你如何尝试与他们建立融洽的关系？

paras.en: I go to work. That’s when it becomes a job, and I treat it as such. I look at it from a place of absolute empathy. It’s not a job for me to sit down and talk to someone if we find something in a mutually curious space. Just stay present, listen to the answer, ask the question and know the music. That’s kind of it. But if someone is struggling, then that’s when you lean into some of the experience you have, but also, I mean, doing this in the ’90s was brutal.
paras.zh: 我去上班。那时它就变成了一份工作，我也这样对待它。我从绝对同理心的角度看待它。如果我们在一个共同好奇的空间中发现了一些东西，那么坐下来与某人交谈并不是我的工作。只需留在现场，聆听答案，提出问题并了解音乐。就是这样。但如果有人正在挣扎，那么你就需要依靠自己的一些经验，而且，我的意思是，在 90 年代这样做是残酷的。

paras.en: I mean, how much time do we have? People would sort of walk in, and they’re like, “Hey, nice to meet you,” and then it starts rolling, and they’re like this [Zane sighs, leans back in his chair, crosses his arms and puts his feet on the table]… [They were] way too cool for me. It was a very cool decade. It was very hard for me to navigate that, but it was a great training ground.
paras.zh: 我的意思是，我们还有多少时间？人们走进来会说，“嘿，很高兴认识你”，然后事情开始滚动，他们就像这样[赞恩叹了口气，靠在椅子上，交叉双臂，把脚放在桌子上]……[他们]对我来说太酷了。这是一个非常酷的十年。对我来说，驾驭这一点非常困难，但这是一个很好的训练场。

paras.en: Do you let guests scrap certain questions in your interviews?
paras.zh: 你会让客人在采访中放弃某些问题吗？

paras.en: Because I’m an artist, a musician. It’s just not my wheelhouse to beat up creative people — and I’m not saying that’s what everyone does. Some people do, but some people are really, really discerning and very critical of art. It’s a really important thing… I really respect anyone who’s in the critical space, who does a good job… I am definitely on the artist side of things…
paras.zh: 因为我是一个艺术家，一个音乐家。我不擅长殴打有创造力的人——我并不是说每个人都这么做。有些人这样做，但有些人对艺术非常非常有洞察力并且非常挑剔。这是一件非常重要的事情……我真的很尊重任何在关键领域、做得很好的人……我绝对站在艺术家一边……

paras.en: I mean, I have no problem telling the truth. I’ve had full conversations that have never come out because the artist has taken me to one side after the fact and had a very heartfelt conversation, very concerned about how they came across. I may not even hear it. I may not even see it. I may not even know what they’re talking about. But that’s where it gets to a place for me where a line is drawn, and I have to ask myself: Why am I doing this? Am I doing this for me, for my career? Am I doing this to say, “No, this is going out”? Because what that really does in that moment is it prioritizes me over the person I spoke with. And that’s something that I’ve always been pretty clear about: I am really just a conduit of curiosity for anyone who wants to share with their audience. It’s not really about me.
paras.zh: 我的意思是，说实话我没有问题。我有过充分的对话，但从未公开，因为艺术家在事后把我带到了一边，进行了一次非常真诚的对话，非常关心他们的印象。我可能连听都没听过。我可能连看都看不到。我什至可能不知道他们在说什么。但这对我来说是一个划定界限的地方，我必须问自己：我为什么要这样做？我这样做是为了我自己，为了我的事业吗？我这样做是不是在说：“不，这要出去了”？因为在那一刻真正起作用的是它优先考虑我而不是与我交谈的人。这是我一直非常清楚的一点：对于任何想要与观众分享的人来说，我实际上只是好奇心的管道。这其实不是关于我的。

paras.en: Tell me about getting started with Apple Music and defining its editorial voice.
paras.zh: 告诉我有关 Apple Music 的入门和定义其编辑声音的信息。

paras.en: When we started the radio here, I didn’t have access or opportunity with a lot of the artists that I built relationships with from the BBC because we were unproven. And I came over here thinking, “Well, I’ve got Jimmy Iovine over here, and I’ve got Apple over here and I feel unstoppable, and who’s not going to want to come and launch this thing with us?” But it was kind of crickets… As upsetting as that was at the time, two good things came out of it. Number one, it snapped me back into the reality force field of building something from scratch. And number two, it made us focus really clearly and in a big way on new and emerging artists. That’s why, if you go back and you actually look at what the first week…my singular world premiere type moment that first week was like Billie Eilish’s “Ocean Eyes.” [Then we did] Khalid’s [American Teen], Bryson Tiller’s first song. These were all first songs by new artists, and we chose them because we had nothing else and we also loved them.
paras.zh: 当我们在这里创办电台时，我没有机会接触到许多与 BBC 建立关系的艺术家，因为我们还没有得到证实。我来到这里想，“好吧，我有 Jimmy Iovine 在这里，我有苹果在这里，我感觉势不可挡，谁不想来和我们一起推出这个东西呢？”但这是一种蟋蟀……尽管当时令人不安，但它产生了两件好事。第一，它让我回到了从头开始构建某些东西的现实力场。第二，它让我们非常清晰地、大力地关注新兴艺术家。这就是为什么，如果你回去看看第一周……我第一周独特的全球首映式时刻就像比莉·艾利什的“海洋之眼”。 [然后我们做了] Khalid 的 [American Teen]，Bryson Tiller 的第一首歌。这些都是新艺术家的第一首歌，我们选择它们是因为我们没有别的，而且我们也喜欢它们。

paras.en: That set us on this path. You know what’s cool? I mean, it’s cool when big artists want to come and do things with you. It’s proof of concept, but what’s really cool is when you get to put your sticker on someone’s flight case, and it’s their first sticker. So it started us on this journey over the last 10 or 11 years where we’ve been building out this radio model.
paras.zh: 这让我们走上了这条道路。你知道什么很酷吗？我的意思是，当大艺术家想来和你一起做事时，这很酷。这是概念验证，但真正酷的是当您将贴纸贴在某人的航空箱上时，这是他们的第一个贴纸。因此，它开启了我们在过去 10 或 11 年里一直在构建这个无线电模型的旅程。

paras.en: We were never, you know, delusional enough to assume we were going to get a huge audience overnight. We’d have to build it like anyone else would have to build anything. But we’ve just got to a point in our 11 years on where we now, overall, reach over 50 million unique listeners a month, which is a really large number for us, and it’s growing exponentially and really fast.
paras.zh: 你知道，我们从来没有妄想到我们会在一夜之间吸引大量观众。我们必须像其他人建造任何东西一样建造它。但在 11 年里，我们已经达到了这样一个阶段：总体而言，我们每个月的独立听众数量超过 5000 万，这对我们来说是一个非常大的数字，而且它正在呈指数级增长，速度非常快。

paras.en: The really cool number is on our radio network. We played — this year alone — over 6,500 individual artists, which is not a commercial radio model. [Other radio networks’] playlists are very small, and the amount of plays is very great. Our playlist is gigantic. We play a lot of different artists, and over half of those 6,500 artists we’ve played in one year are new or emerging. So, think about 3,300 artists, roughly, getting played, who may be on their first song, their first EP, their first album…It’s proof of concept. It’s great.
paras.zh: 非常酷的号码在我们的广播网络上。仅今年一年，我们就与超过 6,500 名个人艺术家合作，这不是商业广播模式。 [其他广播网络]的播放列表很小，但播放量却很大。我们的播放列表非常庞大。我们演奏了很多不同的艺术家，一年内演奏的 6,500 名艺术家中有一半以上都是新人或新兴艺术家。所以，想想大约 3,300 名艺术家，他们可能会出现在他们的第一首歌、他们的第一张 EP、他们的第一张专辑中……这是概念的证明。这很棒。
